law_name: State Budget of the Republic of Bulgaria Act for 2026 (Закон за държавния бюджет на Република България за 2026 г.)
description: The Radev government's budget for 2026, adopted at second reading on 24 July 2026 by 125 votes to 84, sets a deficit of 5.7% of GDP, a ceiling of EUR 10.1 billion for new borrowing (including up to EUR 3.261 billion under the EU SAFE defence instrument), a 10% cut in personnel spending from 1 September, higher tobacco excise and vignette fees, personal social security contributions for civil servants and magistrates, a freeze of the minimum wage at EUR 620.20 and the closure of the commission on the State Security files.
significance: Adopted two weeks after the EU opened an excessive deficit procedure against Bulgaria; on 20 October 2026 the Constitutional Court struck down the minimum-wage freeze, the hours-based calculation of length of service and a new pay formula for junior magistrates, but rejected the request to annul the whole Act.

law_name: Amendments to the Protection of Competition Act and the Consumer Protection Act (June 2026)
description: Tabled by Progressive Bulgaria MPs on 11 May 2026 and adopted at final reading on 11 June 2026, as the government's main response to rising prices. Undertakings in a monopoly, dominant or collective dominant position are barred from charging 'excessively high' prices, with fines of up to 10% of annual turnover imposed by the Commission on Protection of Competition; firms with at least 50% market share (60% jointly) must prove they do not abuse their position; a central electronic register traces agri-food supply chains. The ban on 'economically unjustified' consumer price increases, inherited from the euro adoption law, is extended to August 2027 with higher fines and daily online price publication by large traders.
significance: Delivers the price-control bills Radev announced on taking office; Democratic Bulgaria said in August 2026 that the promise to control prices had not been fulfilled.

law_name: Amendments to the Judicial System Act on the election of a new Supreme Judicial Council (June 2026)
description: Adopted on 25–26 June 2026; the amendments were presented in plenary by Progressive Bulgaria MP Nikoleta Todorova. They set the procedure for electing the new Supreme Judicial Council, whose mandate had long expired, require the elections of members from the judges', prosecutors' and investigators' quota to be held by 17 October 2026, make former presidents of the two supreme courts and former prosecutors general who served during the previous council ineligible, and cap acting terms of the Prosecutor General and the supreme court presidents at six months in total.
significance: The first step of the government's pledge to replace the Supreme Judicial Council and then the Prosecutor General; the parliamentary quota still requires a two-thirds majority.

law_name: Act on Counteracting Corruption among Persons Holding Public Office (2026)
description: Tabled by the outgoing Gyurov caretaker cabinet on 30 April 2026 and adopted under urgent procedure by the new National Assembly, with Progressive Bulgaria's support, at the end of May 2026, to meet a Recovery and Resilience Plan deadline (promulgation by 5 June 2026). It creates a five-member Anti-Corruption Commission whose members are chosen by parliament, the President, the two supreme courts and the Supreme Bar Council, with an annually rotating chair, and lets the Commission challenge in court a prosecutor's refusal to open pre-trial proceedings.
significance: Cited by the European Commission when it released EUR 896 million of Bulgaria's fourth recovery-plan payment. Parliament's member, Plamen Todorov, was elected on 23 July 2026 with Progressive Bulgaria's votes alone (124 to 71).

law_name: Governance Programme of the Republic of Bulgaria 2026–2030 (Програма за управление на Република България 2026–2030 г.)
description: Adopted by the Council of Ministers on 12 August 2026, three months after the government took office, and based on Progressive Bulgaria's election programme. Its 20 chapters open with 'Dismantling the Oligarchic Model and Anti-Corruption Policies' and 'Justice' (restoring the legitimacy of the judiciary, decentralising the prosecution service), followed by fiscal policy and EU funds, administrative optimisation (2026–2027), economy, digital transformation, foreign affairs, security, defence, social policy, education, health, energy (including nuclear expansion) and other sectors.
significance: The reference document for the government's commitments; Democratic Bulgaria described the government's agenda as 'a calendar with wishes instead of a bold and measurable government programme'.

law_name: Cabinet decisions ending arms supplies from army stocks to Ukraine (10 June 2026) and on 'constructive abstention' on the European Peace Facility (21 October 2026)
description: On 10 June 2026 the government discontinued the provision of weapons from Bulgarian armed forces depots to Ukraine. On 21 October 2026 it invoked constructive abstention on the European Peace Facility's financing of new lethal weapons for Ukraine, not blocking the EU decision but directing Bulgaria's mandatory contribution solely to non-lethal assistance, with priority, if possible, for regions of Ukraine where the Bulgarian minority lives.
significance: A reversal of the policy of previous governments since 2022; commercial ammunition exports by Bulgarian manufacturers are not covered.

law_name: Bulgargaz–BOTAS protocol suspending the 2023 gas agreement for 15 months (6 July 2026)
description: Signed after Radev's talks with President Erdoğan in Ankara. For 15 months Bulgargaz pays only for the transmission and regasification capacity it actually uses, under improved commercial terms, instead of the fixed daily fee of about BGN 1 million; the two companies are to renegotiate the contract in line with current market conditions.
significance: Addresses a take-or-pay contract signed under Radev's own caretaker government in 2023; the terms of the final renegotiation and the treatment of some USD 360 million in arrears were not public as of the latest reports.

law_name: 2027 Draft Budgetary Plan submitted to the European Commission and the Eurogroup (15 October 2026)
description: Bulgaria's first draft budgetary plan as a euro-area member targets a general government deficit of 4.3% of GDP in 2027 (after about 5% expected for 2026) and correction of the excessive deficit by 2029. Measures include a one-off windfall contribution in selected sectors (indicative EUR 800 million), an excise duty on motor vehicles, higher gambling taxes and fees, a maximum contributory income of EUR 2,400, tax relief for families with children, about 8% higher pensions, 5% higher public-sector wages and 7.5% higher teachers' salaries.
significance: Sets the fiscal path under the excessive deficit procedure; government debt is projected to rise from about 31.1% to 33.3% of GDP.

law_name: Presidential veto of the law ratifying the agreement to buy F-16 Block 70 fighter jets (2019)
description: On 23 July 2019 President Radev returned to parliament the law ratifying the agreement with the United States for F-16 Block 70 aircraft and related support, arguing that strategic defence decisions needed broad consensus and that the law had been passed on a 'fast track' without two full readings. The National Assembly overrode the veto on 26 July 2019 by 128 votes to 73, with 3 abstentions.
significance: One of his most prominent vetoes in his conflict with the Borisov government; the purchase went ahead.

law_name: Presidential veto of the law ratifying the donation of armoured personnel carriers to Ukraine (2023)
description: On 4 December 2023 Radev returned to parliament the law ratifying the agreement under which Bulgaria provided armoured transport vehicles from Interior Ministry stocks to Ukraine. Prime Minister Nikolai Denkov said he expected parliament to vote the law again; parliament overrode the veto days later.
significance: Illustrates his opposition, as President, to military aid for Ukraine.
